title: Competitor Price Matches and the Registered Limit of Liability under Northgate Protect
content:
**Clause.** Competitor price-match adjustments booked on the covered order line come off the registered limit of liability of a Northgate Protect single-item plan, per unit bought: the whole (100 percent, a share of 1) of a match to a local competitor's advertised price, one half (50 percent, a share of 0.5) of a match to an online competitor's price, and nothing where the line carries no competitor price match.

The adjustments are read from the customer's Northgate Store and Online Orders records: the competitor price-match adjustments booked against the covered order line, the competitor each one matched, the amount each refunded, and the units bought on the line.

## Ladder

| Covered order line carries | Amount that comes off the registered limit |
|---|---|
| A match to a local competitor's advertised price | The whole of the local match amount, divided by the units bought on the line |
| A match to an online competitor's price only | One half of the match amount, divided by the units bought on the line |
| No competitor price match | Nothing |

"Per unit bought" means the match amount refunded on the line is divided by the number of units bought on that line. Where a match to a local competitor's advertised price is booked, it alone determines the amount that comes off.

## Cases on hypothetical figures

- A line of 2 units carries an online competitor match that refunded $30.00. One half is $15.00, and per unit bought $7.50 comes off.
- A line of 1 unit carries a local competitor's advertised-price match that refunded $22.00. The whole $22.00 comes off.
- A line with no competitor price-match adjustment booked against it: nothing comes off.
